failure_summary.description: Four runs left the plain source statement for a single-edit neighbour with an unproved rider: a stronger equivariant isomorphism, a numeric asymptotic coefficient, an 'even without H' clause, and an 'up to scaling / ray' clause. Two runs took a weakened neighbour: one direction only of an iff, and a non-uniform hedge over an FPT bound.
'm=2' was chosen over the logically equivalent congruence form that the other options edit.
A numeric kissing-number record question that depends on recalled knowledge. The run picked a larger, unsupported number.

patch.reasoning: In 5 of the 8 failures (the equivalent-forms item, the isomorphism item, the existence item, the iff item, the periods item), the correct option was the hub: every other option is a one-clause edit of it. Each wrong pick was an ADD-neighbour or a DROP-neighbour of that hub. Step 8 already names the hub test, but it leaves a loophole ('or the hub plus a clause you can derive'), and the stem's superlative ('strongest', 'exact') was read as licence to leave the hub. A longer top-of-document checklist was rejected last step, so I make three short, targeted edits instead. (1) Make the hub step visible and mechanical, say that a superlative is not evidence against the hub, and list exactly when to leave it. (2) Add the one cheap test not yet covered, a symmetry check for structure-preserving 'strengthened isomorphism' riders. (3) Separate 'appended coefficient or expansion' tails from the legitimate 'explicit formula for the named quantity' upgrade, since that overlap seems to have licensed the inflated picks. A final short bullet blocks importing 'unique up to scaling' from a better-known analogous invariant.

edits.target: Override the hub only on positive evidence.
edits.content: Override the hub only on positive evidence. WRITE THE HUB OUT before ranking: name it, then label every other option 'hub + X', 'hub - X' or 'hub with X swapped'. The wrong options are usually its single-edit neighbours. ADD-neighbours look stronger (a rider). DROP-neighbours look safer (one direction of an iff, bare membership, 'only / non-uniform / XP-only' hedges). SWAP-neighbours change a range, object or direction. A superlative in the stem ('strongest', 'exact', 'complete') is NOT evidence against the hub: the hub already is the strongest statement the source proves. Leave the hub only if (i) an ADD-neighbour's extra clause is a standard consequence you can derive in a few lines from the stem's own hypotheses AND is not a coefficient/rate/expansion, a stronger notion of equivalence, a new object, a weakened hypothesis, or a changed quantifier/range; or (ii) you pick a DROP-neighbour because the hub contains a clause that fails a concrete test. If two options are equivalent under the stem's ranges, the hub is the one written in the notation the other options edit.

edits.target: Do not add a ray clause unless the invariant is scale-invariant.
edits.content: - Symmetry/equivariance: an option upgrading 'isomorphic' to 'isomorphic compatibly with the projection, the deck/group action, the labelling, basepoint or orientation' (equivariant, canonical, over the base) is a rider unless the stem asks for it. Test it with a trivial symmetry of the data (relabel by an automorphism of the coefficient group, flip a sign, Galois-conjugate, reparametrize). That symmetry gives an object with the same spectrum or invariant, so the plain-isomorphism statement survives but the structure-preserving one fails.

edits.target: - Options with specific numerics (explicit asymptotic coefficients, exact constants, extra sign or monotonicity claims, a 'moreover' clause on large-time behaviour) are the typical inflated distractors. Keep one only if you can derive the extra detail.
edits.content: - Options with specific numerics (explicit asymptotic coefficients, exact constants, extra sign or monotonicity claims, a 'moreover' clause on large-time behaviour) are the typical inflated distractors. Keep one only if you can derive the extra detail in a few lines. An 'in addition / moreover / as lambda->0' tail that attaches a coefficient, expansion, rate, sign claim or asymptotic-closeness bound to an existence, regularity or membership theorem is a rider. It is NOT the 'explicit formula for the quantity the stem names' upgrade, which applies only when the stem asks for the value or formula of that quantity. 'Even without [a stem hypothesis]' is always the corruption, however strong it looks.

edits.target: Confirm with the stem's naming order or a limiting case (a parameter → 0) when possible.
edits.content: - Do not import a property (invariance under scaling, 'unique up to scaling / ray / normalization', 'unique up to isomorphism') from a better-known analogous invariant. Check it for the stem's own invariant. If the stem never normalizes the objects and the invariant is not shown to be homogeneous of degree 0, state uniqueness plainly.
